unit: board artist and puppet cutter (SCION #29 GrabCut, #2 Reiniger, #41 Secondary Dynamics)

coordinates.angles: deg, + = clockwise on screen (= nose-up for the left-facing glider; legs + = feet forward/left)

glider.note: glider frame, both wings, tail and the pilot's torso and arms (one piece: he is strapped in)

legs.note: legs below the waist; r=15 px blank-card joint cap hidden under the body

glider_core.note: glider without its right (aft) lower wing panel; used from impact on so the wing can droop

glider_wingR.note: outer half of the right lower wing on a pin at its mid-spar (droop at impact)

pilot_torso.note: the pilot alone: head and torso, spars erased and contour re-inked; legs pin at the hip

pilot_arm.note: pilot's right arm on the shoulder pin (flaps the paper wing)

heli_top.note: top rotor (two feather-ribbed blades) on the hub pin

heli_shaft.note: frame and the twisted rubber skein; the band snap is drawn as a pen squiggle from here

heli_bottom.note: bottom rotor (counter-turning) on the lower hub pin

pie_body.note: the commentator (fig. 2, female): body, half-open wings and long tail; branch removed

pie_head.note: head on the neck pin (held angles, bird-like jerks)

fly_body.note: flying magpie (fig. 1, male) body, head and fanned tail; wings cut off at the shoulders

fly_wingL.note: near spread wing on the left shoulder pin (flap = rotation + foreshortening)

fly_wingR.note: far spread wing on the right shoulder pin

pilot_legs.note: the same cut legs piece (board/legs.png) at the pilot's scale

paper_wing_root.note: HANDMADE: cream stock cut with a scalpel-polygon, pen spar and ribs; pinned at the pilot's hand

paper_wing_tip.note: HANDMADE: scalloped tip segment on a crease pin; lags and folds (#41)

dynamics.integrator: semi-implicit (symplectic) Euler, 240 Hz (10 substeps per film frame), sampled per frame, held on 2s

hip_legs.model: pendulum on the hip pin driven by the body's acceleration: phi'' = [-(g - a_y) sin phi + a_x cos phi]/L - c (phi' - theta')
hip_legs.panel_cut_f576: no acceleration across a cut between panels (repair 2)
hip_legs.run_drive: f432-490 legs driven to +-28 deg on 4-frame alternation

paper_wing_tip.model: angular spring-damper relative to the root, inertial drive = -0.9 x arm angular acceleration; crease rest 0 -> 150 deg at f106 (3rd flap)

band_snap.model: whip amplitude spring-damper, impulse 900 px/s at f312

wing_root_droop.model: repair 2: the spar snaps at f605: the outer wing whips to 58 deg, held 3 drawings f605-610, then a spring-damper onto the broken root at 40 deg; joint stop -3..62 (the intact-spar stop is gone)

a1_legs.model: spring to sit pose -80 deg at f150 (25 deg tuck during the hop)

tests_note: measured from the rig and exposure (board.py tests()). pivot drift: child pin vs parent pin in panel px for every joint of every drawing. Repair 2: legs decay measured on the ON-SCREEN run: the body is at rest f540-564 (hang lengthened, slide starts f565); the legs are kicked (6 rad/s) as the body stops dead and must read |phi| >= 8 deg at f542 and < 1 deg by f564. first_failure_frame: first frame with pitch >= 15 deg and x-advance < 0.5 px/frame.

aesthetic_measurements.note: PIL, luminance <120 ink, 120-200 midtone. Wide f700 ink is below the 3 % target because the slip column is still empty here (slips for BB-07/09 come from the writer unit's cues)

Commons searches 'Pica pica Brehms Tierleben', 'Elster Holzstich', 'magpie engraving', 'Bewick magpie' found only whole-book PDFs/DjVu, no single-plate magpie wood engraving in line; a true line-engraved (not lithograph) magpie was not obtained
Higher-resolution Audubon scan (LoC larger TIFF) is marked 'only available at the Library of Congress'; the 385x640 JPEG was used (adequate: the bird is ~90-110 px on screen)
CROW (Corvus scapulatus, Brehms Tierleben, PD) from the test shot is retired: it is a pied crow, not a magpie

repairs.what: joint cap (r=15 px blank card) added above the waist cut so the hip wedge never opens

four spar lines crossing the figure (Hough-detected: [(300, 190, 480, 291), (330, 266, 427, 246), (320, 274, 499, 256), (322, 273, 395, 221)]) erased in a 5 px band; the figure's own contour re-inked across the band by an 11 px closing thinned to pen width (checked visually in pilot_repair_map.png)
hub bar re-inked by hand (68 px pen line, source px) joining the two blades of each rotor across the shaft gap
the plate's single flying pose was cut into body + two wings and re-pinned at the shoulders (Reiniger replacement practice), so the flap cycle is articulated, not a slide

the branch the female perches across (a 23 px band from (163,330) to (276,500)) was inpainted (cv2.INPAINT_TELEA, r=10) and the bird's outline re-inked across the band; she is re-pinned on a pen fence post

inked part labels A (wing) and B (raised nose), graphite dashed horizon through the hip pin and 35 deg arc

known_gaps: the perched magpie (pie_body) is cut from a 385x640 lithograph and printed in two values; it reads as a black-and-white long-tailed bird at film size but its repaired belly (branch removed) is simplified
BB-08 is the only rendered board; BB-00..BB-10 exist in exposure.json as poses (the editor renders them); slips for boards other than BB-08 are the writer unit's
the band snap is a dynamics channel (amplitude per frame in exposure.json a2.band_whip_px); the squiggle itself is to be drawn by the editor from that value
rotor turning is foreshortening (scale_x = |cos phase|) of a flat cut piece, as a paper puppet would be
